entries.finding: The intake path normalizes every open issue into a repository-mutating atom contract or blocks it, so a non-actionable caveat or a disclosed-not-fixed finding cannot exist as an issue; across wave 9 every such item degraded into prose on a record that then closed, and three lanes independently rediscovered the same hole.

entries.finding: ed3c/noodles#272 routed `repair_contract.find_open_pr_for_subject` through `noodles.matching_open_pull_requests`, which makes that function's own `constraint:` comment ("repair_contract.find_open_pr_for_subject does not route through this exit yet") false; the atom declares component `verify` and `policy/component-owners.json` gives `matching_open_pull_requests` to `schedule`, so `component_owner_errors` refuses the candidate that would correct the comment. Any future `schedule`-declared atom touching that definition should delete those four lines.

policy/component-owners.json - `"matching_open_pull_requests": ["schedule"]`
noodles.py:component_owner_errors - refuses a changed definition owned by an undeclared component
tests/test_repair.py::RepairOpenPrCorrelationTests - the routing the comment now contradicts

entries.finding: `tests/test_component_surface.py::ComponentOwnerMapTests.test_noodles_py_unowned_definition_count_matches_the_agents_md_disclosure` pins `assertEqual(len(owned), 18)` on `policy/component-owners.json`, so no candidate can add an owner entry: trusted verify and `./noodles verify --trusted-preview` run the default-branch copy of that test against the candidate's data, exactly the deadlock ed3c/noodles#285 widened out of the sibling assertion in the same method (`assertGreaterEqual(len(defs), 139)`). Reproduced while ed3c/noodles#272 tried to declare `claimed_boundary_widening`'s owner and had to drop the entry instead. Cure is the same one-word widening to a monotonic floor, which still catches a deleted owner entry.
receipts: tests/test_component_surface.py:330 - `self.assertEqual(len(owned), 18)`
tests/test_component_surface.py:318-325 - the ed3c/noodles#285 docstring naming this exact deadlock for the sibling assertion
reproduce: add one entry to policy/component-owners.json, then PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m unittest tests.test_component_surface -> `AssertionError: 19 != 18`

entries.finding: `tests/test_schedule_contract.py::ScheduleContractTests.run_carrier` defaults `root=CANDIDATE_ROOT` and runs `.agents/bin/codex` with `cwd=CANDIDATE_ROOT`, so the carrier's own `isolated_home.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` writes `.noodle/codex-isolation/{home,codex-home}` into the live checkout - `.noodle/` runtime state written by a test outside its own temporary directory, the exact class every atom's acceptance clause forbids. `.gitignore:3` keeps it out of any commit, so no candidate has ever been rejected for it and nothing reds. Cure: pass a `copy_tracked` root, which `mutated_copy` in the same class already builds.
receipts: tests/test_schedule_contract.py:77 - `def run_carrier(self, argv, root: Path = CANDIDATE_ROOT)`, invoked at line 92 with `cwd=root`
.agents/bin/codex:137-138 - `isolated_home.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)`
reproduce: rm -rf .noodle/codex-isolation && PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m unittest tests.test_schedule_contract && ls .noodle -> `codex-isolation` reappears
